title: DKA 7 of 7, high-risk antepartum unit: type 1 diabetes in pregnancy at 28 weeks, DKA at a glucose of 242, potassium 3.2 on insulin, Category II fetal tracing, morning low glucose, evening contractions and the betamethasone decision (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis in pregnancy at 28 weeks 2 days (glucose 242, venous pH 7.24, bicarbonate 10, anion gap 26, BHB 5.4) in type 1 diabetes after gastroenteritis and a halved basal insulin dose; potassium 3.2 and magnesium 1.5 on the insulin (short hold, dextrose kept, two peripheral KCl riders); Category II fetal heart rate tracing that clears as the mother is corrected (no emergent cesarean); fasting hypoglycemia on the first full basal dose; Day 2 evening contractions with negative fetal fibronectin and cervical length 3.8 cm (no betamethasone)
desc: Mon 12/28 0700 to Thu 12/31 0700. A 29-year-old with type 1 diabetes, 28 weeks pregnant, arrives on the high-risk antepartum unit in DKA at a glucose of only 242 with fetal monitoring running; care covers the potassium drop on insulin, keeping dextrose for the baby, left lateral positioning, a morning low, evening contractions and sick-day teaching. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
